mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within three months indicates a tightening labor market, which increases wage costs and boosts consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.5% within three months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real estate sales (HOUST) by more than 5% in a month signals increased consumer confidence and economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% signals increased economic output, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the periods with sustained 3-month increases in INDPRO by more than 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% in the same month, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real disposable personal income (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a month signals reduced consumer spending, which decreases corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS decreased by more than 1% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) increases by more than 2% in a quarter and industrial production (INDPRO) also increases by more than 1% in the same quarter, it signals robust economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 2% and INDPRO increases > 1% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where GDPC1 increased by more than 2% and INDPRO increased by more than 1% within a quarter.
